title: Food set before gods that cannot eat.
subtitle: Offerings to things that cannot receive
then: Ibn Kathir says the people {trap}had placed food before the idols as a sacrifice, so that the food might be blessed{/trap}. When Ibrahim saw it, he asked them: will you not eat? The question showed how helpless they were.
now: You give your best hours to things that give nothing back. The lucky charm on the mirror, the brand you trust more than your prayer. {idea}Ask them: can you actually do anything for me?{/idea}
old: Some things bring luck or blessing on their own.
new: Only Allah gives blessing. Everything else needs Him as much as I do.
try: Notice one thing you treat as lucky or protective. Remind yourself today that blessing is from Allah alone.

title: Why do you not answer? They had nothing to say.
subtitle: A god that cannot speak cannot guide

key.label: What you should ask of a god

then: Standing alone among the idols, Ibrahim asked {idea}what is the matter with you that you speak not?{/idea} The food sat untouched. The statues stayed silent. Their silence was the whole argument.
now: In the hospital corridor, your savings, your connections, your title cannot say a word to you. {idea}Allah hears the whisper you cannot even say out loud.{/idea} Turn to the One who answers.
old: What I rely on will be there for me when it counts.
new: Only Allah hears and answers. Everything else goes silent when I need it most.
try: Next time you are worried today, speak to Allah first before reaching for anything else.

title: He struck the idols with his strong right hand.
subtitle: Breaking what had been worshipped

key.label: How to deal with an idol

then: Ibn Kathir says Ibrahim {idea}hit them with his right hand because it is stronger{/idea}, and left them broken to pieces, except the biggest, so the people might turn to it. The full story is told in Surat Al-Anbiya'.
now: You do not need to break anyone else's things. Look at your own idols: the app that owns your nights, the habit that comes before prayer. {idea}Half measures keep it standing.{/idea} Use your strong hand.
old: I will cut back slowly on what pulls me from Allah.
new: Some things in my life need a decisive break, not a slow negotiation.
try: Remove one thing today that keeps pulling you from Allah. Delete it, give it away, or block it.

title: The crowd came rushing back at him.
subtitle: When you break with the group, the group comes
then: Mujahid said the word means {trap}they came rushing{/trap}. Ibn Kathir notes they did not know at first who had done it, until they looked into it and found it was Ibrahim. Then they came to rebuke him.
now: You stop joining in the gossip, and suddenly the group chat goes quiet, then turns on you. {trap}Everyone wants an explanation.{/trap} {idea}You do not have to panic. You can answer calmly and stay where you are.{/idea}
old: If many people come at me, I must have done something wrong.
new: Pressure from many does not make the truth wrong. I can stay calm.
try: If someone pushes back on a good choice of yours today, answer in one calm sentence and leave it there.

title: You bow to what your own hands carved?
subtitle: Worshipping something you made yourself
then: When they came to rebuke him, Ibrahim turned it back on them. Ibn Kathir says he meant: {trap}do you worship idols which you yourselves carve and fashion with your own hands?{/trap}
now: You built the career, the image, the house, the follower count. Now you check it, fear for it, and give up sleep for it. {trap}Your own work has become your master.{/trap} {idea}Things you made should serve you, while you serve Allah.{/idea}
old: What I built is mine to protect at any cost.
new: What I make should never become what I bow to.
try: Name one thing you built that now controls you. Set one limit on it today.

title: Allah made you, and also what you make.
subtitle: Even your work is His creation
then: Ibn Kathir says this may mean Allah created you and what you do, or you and what you make, and {idea}both views are synonymous{/idea}. The carvers and their carvings are both created. So how can one be worshipped?
now: The app you coded, the cake you baked, the report your boss praised. {idea}The skill, the hands, the idea, the materials: all made by Allah.{/idea} That does not shrink your effort. It gives it a place to bow.
old: What I make comes from me alone.
new: My skill and my work are both created by Allah. That is a reason to thank Him.
try: After you finish one piece of work today, say alhamdulillah and mean it.

title: When they lost the argument, they built a fire.
subtitle: Force is what is left when proof is gone
then: Ibn Kathir says {trap}when the proof had been established against them, they resolved to seize him by force{/trap}. They said: build him a structure and throw him into the blazing fire. Allah saved him, as told in Surat Al-Anbiya'.
now: You are losing an argument with your spouse, your sibling, your coworker. You feel the urge to get louder, to threaten, to bring up old wounds. {trap}That is the fire-building move.{/trap} {idea}The braver move is to admit they might be right.{/idea}
old: When I am losing, I need to push harder.
new: When I have no answer, the honest thing is to listen, not to get louder.
try: The next time you lose a point in a disagreement today, say: you have a fair point.

title: They planned against him, and ended up the lowest.
subtitle: The plot turned upside down
then: Ibn Kathir says {reward}Allah saved him from the fire and caused him to prevail over them{/reward}, making his proof supreme. The people who planned to destroy him became the lowest.
now: Someone at work is building a case against you. A relative is spreading a story. You lie awake running through every move they could make. {idea}They have plans. Allah has the final one.{/idea} Keep doing right.
old: If people are plotting against me, I must out-plot them.
new: I do what is right and leave the plotters to Allah. He has the last move.
try: Tonight, name the situation in a short du'a and hand it over. Then sleep.

title: I am going to my Lord. He will guide me.
subtitle: Leaving with no map but trust
then: Ibn Kathir says after Allah helped Ibrahim against his people, and {trap}after he gave up hoping they would ever believe{/trap}, he emigrated away from them. He did not name a city. He named his Lord.
now: You are leaving a job that compromised your faith, moving away from a crowd that was dragging you down. You do not know what is next. {idea}Ibrahim did not either.{/idea} He just knew Who he was going to.
old: I cannot leave until I know exactly where I am going.
new: If I am leaving for Allah's sake, I can trust Him to show me the way.
try: If you are facing a change for Allah's sake, say his words today: I am going to my Lord, He will guide me.

title: Alone in a new land, he asked for righteous family.
subtitle: A prayer to replace what he left behind
then: Ibn Kathir explains Ibrahim asked for {reward}obedient children, in compensation for his people and relatives whom he had left{/reward}. He had given up his family for Allah, and he asked Allah for a new one.
now: You moved away for work and the family group chat feels far. Or you are hoping to marry, or to have a child. {idea}Ask Allah not just for people, but for righteous ones.{/idea} That is what Ibrahim asked for.
old: I just want a family. Character can come later.
new: When I ask for family, I ask for righteousness first.
try: Add this short du'a to your prayer today: my Lord, grant me from the righteous.

title: The good news of a forbearing boy.
subtitle: Isma'il, named by his character before his trial

row.title: forbearing
sub: the trait the test will need

then: Ibn Kathir says {reward}this child was Isma'il{/reward}, the first son whose birth was announced to Ibrahim, older than Ishaq. He notes Ibrahim was eighty-six when Isma'il was born. The boy is described as forbearing before anything else happens.
now: Think of the people you love. What is the one quality you would thank Allah for in each of them? {idea}Character is a gift, not just a skill.{/idea} The patience in a child is a blessing to name and nurture.
old: Children are a blessing because of what they achieve.
new: A child's gentle, patient character is itself the good news.
try: Tell a child or young person in your life one good quality you see in them today.

title: A father asks his son what he thinks.
subtitle: The hardest command, met with a conversation

row.title: Ibrahim
sub: so look, what do you think?

then: 'Ubayd bin 'Umayr said {idea}the dreams of the Prophets are revelation{/idea}, so this was a command from Allah to a Prophet. Ibn Kathir says Ibrahim told his son to make it easier for him and to test his patience. The young man answered: if Allah wills, you will find me patient.
now: This was a unique test for a Prophet, not a pattern for anyone. But notice how he did it. A hard family decision, a move abroad, a sickness. {idea}He did not hide it. He asked: what do you think?{/idea}
old: Hard decisions are for me to make alone and announce.
new: Even the hardest news is easier to carry when shared with honest conversation.
try: In one family decision this week, ask the person most affected: what do you think?

title: Both of them submitted. That was the real moment.
subtitle: When surrender is complete on both sides
then: Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Qatadah and others said {idea}they submitted and followed the command of Allah{/idea}: Ibrahim obeyed Allah, and Isma'il obeyed Allah and his father. Ibn Kathir says he laid him face down so he would not have to see his face.
now: There is a moment when you stop arguing with Allah's decree. After the diagnosis. After the job is gone. {idea}The heart says yes, even before you know how it ends.{/idea} That yes is what the test was looking for.
old: Submitting means I have no feelings about it.
new: Submitting is choosing Allah's way with my heart, even while it is hard.
try: Name one thing you are still arguing with Allah about. Say quietly: I accept, help me through it.

title: At the very edge, a voice called his name.
subtitle: O Ibrahim: relief that arrives at the last moment
then: In the report from Ibn 'Abbas, Ibrahim had laid his son down and {reward}then he was called from behind{/reward}. He turned and saw a fine, horned, white ram. The call came exactly when the obedience was complete.
now: You have been praying for months. The rent is due tomorrow. The results come in an hour. {idea}Help often comes at the edge, not before it.{/idea} Allah knows your name and your moment.
old: If help has not come yet, it is not coming.
new: Allah's relief can arrive at the last moment, and it is never late.
try: If you are waiting on something hard today, keep doing your part and say: Allah knows my moment.

title: You have fulfilled the vision. This is how Allah rewards.
subtitle: Obedience in hard things opens a way out

row.title: a way out
sub: for those who obey in hard things

then: Ibn Kathir says the purpose of the dream was {idea}fulfilled by his laying down his son{/idea}. Then: this is how We deal with those who obey Us in difficult things; {reward}We make for them a way out{/reward}. He links it to 65:2-3.
now: You turned down the haram money, and now the bills are tight. You kept your word when it cost you. {idea}Allah sees the willingness, not just the result.{/idea} And He promises a way out for that kind of person.
old: If I obey Allah in this, I will only lose.
new: When I obey Allah in something hard, He opens a way I could not see.
try: Do one hard right thing today that you have been avoiding. Trust the way out.
